findings.finding: Inderes' Q3 preview forecasts comparable EBIT of EUR182m against a compiled consensus of EUR209m (adj. EPS 0.23 vs 0.29) and says consensus sets the bar high relative to market conditions, with weak pricing power, Energy down on the OL3 outage and Leuna/Lappeenranta losses.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Inderes made the same 'consensus optimistic' call before Q4 2025 and UPM beat by ~33% on EPS, stock +6.28% on 2026-02-04; before Q2 2026 Inderes feared the H2 guide and was right, stock -7.76% on 2026-07-23. Q3 prints moved +0.13% (2025-10-29) and -2.10% (2024-10-29).
findings.original_quote: Ennustamme UPM:n oikaistun liikevoiton nousseen Q3:lla vajaat 20 % 182 MEUR:oon. Vaatimatonta tulostasoa peilaava ennusteemme on konsensuksen alapuolella. [We forecast UPM's adjusted EBIT rose just under 20% to EUR182m in Q3. Our forecast, reflecting a modest earnings level, is below consensus.]
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public preview from the most-read Finnish retail research house, so part of it is in the price; but the 209 consensus it quotes is the bar the release will be read against, and the stock has drifted only -1.4% over 20 sessions, which is not what a market that had marked the quarter down to 182 would look like. If it were priced, consensus itself would have converged toward 182.
findings.independence: OP cut its UPM target by EUR0.50 to EUR28.0 (Buy) on 2026-10-20, consistent with estimate trimming into the print (reported on the Inderes forum, https://forum.inderes.com/t/sellulove-eli-stora-upm-metsa-jne/725, post 4380); otherwise none.

findings.finding: Peer read before the print is soft: SCA's Q3 report (2026-10-23) says the pulp market remained weak and European NBSK prices fell slightly in Q3, partly offset by lower raw-material costs; Holmen (2026-10-22) missed consensus on Board & Paper; Billerud only slightly beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UPM's Q2 commentary credited a 'moderate increase in pulp prices'; its H2 outlook assumes moderately higher sales prices vs H1, so flat-to-lower Q3 pulp cuts against the company's own guide wording. No clean history of UPM reacting to a peer pulp read.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: pulp indices are public and analysts update for them. The residual is that UPM guided to higher H2 prices and the counterparty evidence says Q3 pulp did not rise; UPM's own net softwood exposure (Fibres North) is the part the 'moderately higher prices' assumption leaned on. Net of the rest: Uruguay hardwood, Energy, Biofuels and Advanced Materials are ~two thirds of EBIT and this read says nothing about them, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Holmen Q3 miss vs Bloomberg consensus SEK637m operating profit (https://www.placera.se/telegram/holmen-holmen-vantas-redovisa-637-miljoner-kronor-i-rorelseresultat-bloomberg-20261020); Inderes forum notes on Billerud/Holmen (https://forum.inderes.com/t/sellulove-eli-stora-upm-metsa-jne/725, posts 4381-4382); Maaseudun Tulevaisuus 2026-10-27 on the Chinese softwood pulp surge (paywalled, cited via forum post 4390).

findings.finding: Inderes expects UPM to address long-term nuclear-power PPAs with data-centre operators on results day, a narrative UPM's stock has already shown sensitivity to (UPM +5.39% on 2026-09-09, the day Google announced EUR13bn data-centre and energy investments in Finland).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UPM +5.39% on 2026-09-09 on the Google Finland data-centre news (Yahoo daily bars); no prior UPM-specific PPA announcement to compare.
findings.original_quote: Pidemmällä tähtäimellä UPM:llä olisi mielestämme mahdollisuuksia tehdä Fortumin tavoin pitkäaikaisia PPA-sopimuksia ydinvoimatuotannostaan datakeskustoimijoiden kanssa, mitä yhtiö tulee arviomme mukaan myös sivuamaan tulospäivänä tavalla tai toisella. [Longer term UPM could, like Fortum, sign long-term PPAs on its nuclear output with data-centre operators, which we expect the company to touch on one way or another on results day.]
findings.why_not_priced: An inference about call commentary, not a document; it is an option the price does not hold as a contract because none has been announced. If a PPA were expected for the release, UPM would not be trading flat into it.
findings.independence: Inderes forum post 69575 (2026-10-06) and post 30649 (2026-09-09) on UPM Energy's data-centre optionality (https://forum.inderes.com/t/sellulove-eli-stora-upm-metsa-jne/725 search results); weak.

baseline_tension: Agrees weakly with nothing: the lean (+0.07) and run-up (-1.4% 20d) are flat, and the findings lean slightly negative on public broker and peer evidence, so there is no positioning or run-up to beat or agree with.
language_note: The only sourced Q3 consensus (EUR209m comparable EBIT, range 175-226, adj. EPS 0.29) came from Inderes' Finnish-language preview; English searches returned no Q3 2026 consensus at all.
Inderes' Finnish preview carried the analyst's below-consensus EUR182m and the expectation of PPA commentary; neither appeared in English sources.

The Finnish Inderes forum carried the OP target cut (EUR28.0) and the Holmen/Billerud read-through notes, and the Maaseudun Tulevaisuus piece on the Chinese softwood pulp surge (paywalled); English wire copy carried none of these.
The company's own releases (results timing, EU Commission letter, WISA listing) were bilingual and the Finnish versions added nothing.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'too small about the move': the release is not pre-released and a narrowing of the EUR200m-wide H2 range is plausible, so abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5; p_up left at 45 because the evidence is a public preview and a peer proxy.
'A truncated zero is not a disclosure': positioning_check states anchor_covered false and that the zero is the 0.5% floor.
'Session check opens with the verdict and a timestamp': session_check rewritten to open with bmo and cite the issuer's 09:30-10:00 EET timing.
Finding sizes unchanged: no lesson argued for moving any of the three.
